title: Structured discovery
task_statement: Turn stakeholder requests into measurable requirements, owners, and prohibited behaviors before design starts. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Success criteria and evaluation sets
components.first_principle: A requirement becomes testable only when it has a metric, a threshold, and a named scope.

nodes.label: Success criterion with metric and threshold
Evaluation set from real task distribution

steps: Write each requirement as a specific and measurable criterion.
Attach a quantitative metric or a defined qualitative scale to each criterion.
Name the owner who accepts each threshold. (Inference)
Build a test set that mirrors the real task distribution.
Add edge cases to the test set.
Score each output with code, an LLM, or a human scorer.
Compare the measured result with the threshold before design starts. (Inference)
pros: Turns vague goals into checks that a team can run.
Gives every stakeholder the same pass or fail test. (Inference)
Shows which requirement fails before release. (Inference)
cons: Thresholds need data that the team may not have yet. (Inference)
Each quality dimension adds its own evaluation work. (Inference)
Human scoring is slow and expensive, so the docs advise against it when possible.
use_when: A request uses adjectives such as accurate or fast.
The team builds an LLM feature with a measurable quality bar.
Several success criteria must hold at the same time.
do_not_use_when: A throwaway prototype needs no pass or fail bar. (Inference)
No representative inputs exist, so the test set cannot mirror the task. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set an acceptable response time as a criterion, based on real-time needs.
constraints.combination: Add a percentile target, such as 95 percent of responses under a limit, when the average hides slow requests.

constraints.choice: Set a budget for each call or each month as a criterion.
constraints.combination: Compare options by cost per completed task when quality differs. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name a signed owner for each threshold. (Inference)
Record operational criteria such as response time and uptime.

components.exam_tie: D6.1. Expect a vague stakeholder request with no metric. The credited answer defines measurable criteria before any design. (Inference)
components.trap: Design built on adjectives such as fast looks efficient, but no one can test it, so the team builds to a guessed bar. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Convert each adjective into a metric, a threshold, and an owner before design.
components.exam_tip: If the stem gives adjectives but no metric, the first action is discovery.

key_facts.text: Good success criteria are specific, measurable, achievable, and relevant.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Most use cases need multidimensional evaluation along several success criteria.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Common success criteria include task fidelity, latency, and price.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Eval design favors test sets that mirror the real task distribution and include edge cases.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Code-based grades are the fastest and most reliable, and human grades are slow and expensive.
key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Discovery question grid
components.first_principle: Each question covers one dimension where a silent assumption can hide. (Inference)
steps: List the dimensions that can hide assumptions, such as prohibitions, cost, volume, and compliance. (Inference)
Ask the owner of each dimension one question. (Inference)
Record each answer with its date and the name of the person who gave it. (Inference)
Log each unconfirmed guess as an open assumption. (Inference)
Close every open assumption before the design gate. (Inference)
pros: Surfaces prohibited behaviors before the build starts. (Inference)
Exposes answers that disagree across owners early. (Inference)
Costs little compared with rework after a demo. (Inference)
cons: Stakeholders may not know the corner cases either. (Inference)
Answers go stale when volume or compliance changes. (Inference)
use_when: A request names outcomes but no limits, owners, or volumes. (Inference)
The system touches money, personal data, or several teams. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: A short internal demo uses no real data. (Inference)
The requirement is one fixed setting with an obvious owner. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name one owner who signs each requirement. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Add a review date to every signed answer. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Record expected volume, with peak bursts. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Recheck the volume answer after a growth event. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set a workspace spend limit that enforces the cost answer.
Name the on-call owner for each operational dependency. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D6.1. Expect a scenario with an unanswered requirement. The credited answer runs discovery before any design. (Inference)
components.trap: Feature work first looks productive, but an unanswered limit still breaks the first production demo. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Ask one question for each dimension, and do not design around a blank answer. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: A blank answer is an open risk, so name the owner who fills it.

key_facts.text: Workspace spend limits cap monthly spending for one workspace.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Spend limits cannot be set on the Default Workspace.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Requirement has metric and threshold?} -->|No| B[Ask the owner for a number]
  B --> A
  A -->|Yes| C{Owner signed the threshold?}
  C -->|No| D[Log open assumption]
  D --> B
  C -->|Yes| E{Prohibited behaviors listed?}
  E -->|No| F[Ask the owner for prohibitions]
  F --> E
  E -->|Yes| G[Build test set and start design]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  A[Adjective] --> B[Metric]
  B --> C[Threshold]
  C --> D[Owner signs]
  D --> E[Test set]
  E --> F[Scored result]
  A --> G[Open assumption]
  G --> D

patterns.wording: a request with adjectives but no metric or threshold
patterns.rule: Convert each adjective into a metric, a threshold, and an owner.
traps: Build a prototype and tune the wording later

patterns.wording: a requirement that names no prohibited behavior
patterns.answer_type: written prohibition in the requirement record
patterns.rule: Write each prohibited behavior as a design constraint with a named owner.
traps: Rely on a reviewer to catch it later

patterns.wording: an owner who is unknown or who changed roles
patterns.answer_type: named owner who signs the requirement
patterns.rule: Assign one owner who signs each requirement before design.
traps: Leave the sign-off with the whole team
